source_refs.note: Book pp. 14-15: printed heading "1.4 Polar Coordinates System" (number misprinted), polar grid, rectangular vs polar figure, P(5, pi/4), Q(-5, pi/4) and the Note

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ne is heading ka number 1.4 likha hai, lekin 1.4 to pehle hi "Three Cube Roots of Unity" (kitab ka page 12) ka number hai. Is ke baad wali headings ke numbers (1.4.1, 1.3.3 aur 1.5) bhi dobara aa gaye hain. Hum ne numbers bilkul kitab jaise rakhe hain taa ke aap apni kitab mein yeh hissa foran dhoond saken. Pareshan na hon: ghalti sirf numbering mein hai, maths bilkul theek hai.

Is sabaq mein hum ek naya tareeqa seekhenge jis se kisi point ki jagah batayi jaati hai: polar coordinates. Pichli classes mein aap ne Cartesian (rectangular) coordinates parhe the, aur is unit mein Argand diagram par complex number \(z = x + iy\) ko point \((x, y)\) bana kar plot bhi kiya tha. Ab hum usi point ko ek doosre andaaz se describe karna seekhenge. Aage chal kar (1.4.1 aur 1.3.3 mein) yahi tareeqa complex numbers ko multiply aur divide karna bohat aasan bana dega, is liye isay dhyan se samajhiye.

Pehle yaad kijiye ke Cartesian coordinates kaise kaam karte hain. Ordered pair \((x, y)\) humein do hidaayat deta hai: pehle \(x\)-axis ke saath \(x\) units chaliye, phir \(y\) units upar (ya \(y\) negative ho to neeche) jaiye. Yeh bilkul aise hai jaise kisi sheher ka naqsha jis mein seedhi sadkein hon: "do block mashriq ki taraf, phir teen block shimaal ki taraf."
Polar coordinates yahi kaam ek aur tareeqe se karte hain. Woh poochte hain: point ek fixed point se kitni door hai, aur kis direction (simt) mein hai? Yaani "kitni door aur kis taraf". Jaise koi aap se raasta poochhe to aap haath se ishara kar ke kehte hain: "us taraf, taqreeban do kilometre."
Kitab batati hai ke jab kisi situation mein circular ya rotational symmetry ho (yaani cheez gol ho ya kisi markaz ke gird ghoomti ho, jaise pankha, ghari ki suiyan, radar), ya sawal kisi fixed point se distance aur ek reference direction se angle par depend kare, to polar coordinates Cartesian se zyada aasan aur qudrati rehte hain.

blocks.alt: Polar grid: concentric circles of radius 1 to 4 around the pole O, the polar axis to the right marked 0 degrees, rays labelled pi/4 (45 degrees), pi/2 (90 degrees), 3pi/4 (135 degrees), pi (180 degrees), 5pi/4 (225 degrees), 3pi/2 (270 degrees) and 7pi/4 (315 degrees), and a point P(r, theta) on the pi/4 ray at distance r from O.
blocks.caption: Figure: the polar grid, with the pole O, the polar axis and a point P(r, θ) (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text:
Ab upar wali figure ko dhyan se dekhiye. Yeh polar grid hai. Is mein seedhi lines ka jaal nahi, balkay ek hi markaz ke gird daire (circles) hain aur markaz se nikalti hui shuaain (rays) hain. Polar coordinate system mein kisi point ki position do numbers se fix hoti hai:
1. ek directed distance \(r\), ek fixed origin \(O\) se. Is \(O\) ko pole (markazi nuqta) kehte hain. Directed ka matlab hai ke is distance ke saath direction ka sign bhi juda hota hai (is ki tafseel neeche "Positive aur negative r" mein aayegi).
2. ek angle \(\theta\), jo pole ko point se milane wali line polar axis ke saath banati hai. Polar axis pole se nikalne wali ek fixed ray (seedhi lakeer jo ek taraf chalti jaati hai) hai, aur aam taur par isay positive \(x\)-axis ke saath rakha jata hai.
Figure mein daire batate hain ke point pole se kitni door hai (radius 1, 2, 3, 4), aur rays batati hain ke kis angle par hai (\(0\), \(\pi/4\), \(\pi/2\), ... ). Point \(P(r, \theta)\) us jagah hai jahan \(r\) radius wala daira aur \(\theta\) angle wali ray milte hain.

Is tarah polar coordinate system mein kisi point \(P\) ki location ko \((r, \theta)\) ki shakal mein likhte hain, jahan \(r\) aur \(\theta\) dono real numbers hain. Dhyan dijiye ke likhne ka order fixed hai: pehle distance \(r\), phir angle \(\theta\). Agar aap order ulta likh dein to bilkul doosra point ban jaayega.

blocks.alt: Left: rectangular coordinates, point P(x, y) reached by going x along the x-axis and y up. Right: polar coordinates, the same kind of point P(r, theta) reached by a segment of length r from O making angle theta with the polar axis.
blocks.caption: Figure: a point in rectangular coordinates (x, y) and in polar coordinates (r, θ) (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text: Ab dono figures ka muqabla kijiye. Baayen taraf rectangular coordinates hain: point \(P(x, y)\) tak pohanchne ke liye pehle \(x\) units right chalte hain, phir \(y\) units upar; do seedhe qadam jo aapas mein right angle banate hain. Daayen taraf polar coordinates hain: wahi kaam ek hi seedhe qadam se hota hai. Pole \(O\) se \(\theta\) angle ki taraf munh kijiye aur seedha \(r\) units chal dijiye. Point aik hi hai, sirf usay batane ka tareeqa badla hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Ek misaal se samajhiye. Socho samundar mein ek lighthouse hai aur aap kisi dost ko ek kashti ki jagah batana chahte hain. Aap keh sakte hain: "kashti lighthouse se 5 km door hai, mashriq (east) se \(45^{\circ}\) ki direction mein." Bas, yahi polar coordinate hai: \(r = 5\) aur \(\theta = 45^{\circ}\). Lighthouse pole hai aur mashriq wali direction polar axis.
Do baatein yaad rakhiye:
• Angle hamesha polar axis se counter-clockwise (ghari ki suiyon ke ulat taraf) naapa jata hai. Clockwise naapa gaya angle negative likha jata hai.
• Is unit mein angles aksar radians mein likhe jate hain. Bunyaadi rishta yeh hai: \(\pi\) radians \(= 180^{\circ}\). Is liye kisi bhi angle ko degrees se radians mein badalne ke liye \(\pi/180\) se multiply kijiye, aur radians se degrees mein badalne ke liye \(180/\pi\) se.
Neeche wali table zubani yaad kar lijiye; poori unit (aur agle saal tak) bohat kaam aayegi.

blocks.caption: Teaching table (hamari taraf se): aam angles degrees aur radians mein

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Table dekh kar khud bataiye: \(120^{\circ}\) radians mein kitna hoga? Aur \(5\pi/6\) degrees mein kitna? (Jawab: \(120 \times \pi/180 = 2\pi/3\), aur \(5 \times 180/6 = 150^{\circ}\).) Agar aap ne yeh khud nikaal liya to aap aage ke liye tayyar hain.

Ab ek dilchasp baat. Aam taur par hum \(r\) ko non-negative (\(r \ge 0\)) lete hain, kyun ke distance aam zindagi mein negative nahi hota. Lekin polar coordinates mein \(r\) negative (\(r < 0\)) bhi ho sakta hai, aur is ka ek saaf matlab hai. \(r\) ka sign badalne se point ki jagah badal jaati hai, is liye dono soorton ko alag alag samajhte hain.
Pehli soorat, jab \(r > 0\) ho: angle \(\theta\) standard position mein koi bhi aisa angle hai jis ki terminal side (aakhri bazu) pole se point \(P\) tak jaane wali line ke saath ho, aur yeh polar axis (positive \(x\)-axis) se counter-clockwise naapa jata hai. Aasan alfaaz mein: polar axis se \(\theta\) angle tak ghoomiye, phir usi direction mein seedha \(r\) units chal dijiye. Wahi point \(P\) hai.
Misaal: polar coordinates \((5, \pi/4)\) ka matlab hai ek point jo pole se 5 units door hai aur \(\pi/4\) radians, yaani \(45^{\circ}\), ke angle par hai. Neeche figure mein yeh point first quadrant mein hai, \(x\)-axis aur \(y\)-axis ke bilkul darmiyan wali line par.

blocks.alt: The point P(5, pi/4): a segment of length 5 from the pole O at an angle of pi/4 above the polar axis.
blocks.caption: Figure: P(5, π/4) is 5 units from the pole at angle π/4 (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text:
Doosri soorat, jab \(r < 0\) ho: angle \(\theta\) ab bhi usi line ka angle hai jo pole se guzarti hai, lekin point \(Q\) us direction mein nahi balkay bilkul ulti direction mein \(|r|\) units par hota hai. Ulti direction ka angle \(\theta + \pi\) hai, kyun ke \(\pi\) radians (\(180^{\circ}\)) ghoomne se munh bilkul peeche ki taraf ho jata hai.
Is ko aise sochiye: aap \(\theta\) ki taraf munh kar ke khade hain. \(r\) positive ho to aage chaliye; \(r\) negative ho to munh wahi rakhiye lekin ulte qadmon peeche chaliye. Aap pole ki doosri taraf pohanch jaayenge.
Misaal: polar coordinates \((-5, \pi/4)\) ka matlab hai ek point jo pole se 5 units door hai, lekin is direction mein:
\[\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \pi = \dfrac{5\pi}{4} \text{ radians.}\]
\(5\pi/4 = 225^{\circ}\), is liye yeh point third quadrant mein aata hai, bilkul \((5, \pi/4)\) ke saamne, pole ki doosri taraf.

blocks.alt: The point Q(-5, pi/4): the ray at angle pi/4 is dashed; Q lies 5 units from O in the opposite direction, at angle pi/4 + pi = 5pi/4, in the third quadrant. An arc shows the turn of 5pi/4 from the polar axis.
blocks.caption: Figure: Q(−5, π/4) lies 5 units from the pole in the direction π/4 + π = 5π/4 (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: \((-5, \pi/4)\) aur \((5, 5\pi/4)\) plane mein ek hi point hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kitab ka yeh Note pehli nazar mein ajeeb lagta hai: do mukhtalif pairs aur point ek? Aaiye isay tasdeeq karte hain. Dono ko rectangular coordinates mein badal kar dekhte hain. Is ke liye formula \(x = r\cos\theta\), \(y = r\sin\theta\) use hoga (yeh formula agle topic 1.4.1 mein figure se saabit kiya jayega; abhi bas isay istemaal kijiye).
\((-5, \pi/4)\) ke liye:
\[x = -5\cos\tfrac{\pi}{4} = -\tfrac{5}{\sqrt{2}}\]
\[y = -5\sin\tfrac{\pi}{4} = -\tfrac{5}{\sqrt{2}}\]
\((5, 5\pi/4)\) ke liye:
\[x = 5\cos\tfrac{5\pi}{4} = -\tfrac{5}{\sqrt{2}}\]
\[y = 5\sin\tfrac{5\pi}{4} = -\tfrac{5}{\sqrt{2}}\]
Dekha? Dono se \(x = y = -\tfrac{5}{\sqrt{2}} \approx -3.54\) aata hai, yaani third quadrant ka bilkul wahi point. Pehli soorat mein minus sign \(r\) ke saath tha, doosri mein \(\cos\) aur \(\sin\) khud negative ho gaye; nateeja ek hi hai.
Ek aur baat: poora chakkar \(2\pi\) (yaani \(360^{\circ}\)) ghoom kar aap wapas usi direction mein aa jaate hain, jaise ghari ki sui 12 se chal kar poora chakkar laga kar phir 12 par aa jaati hai. Is liye \((5, \pi/4)\), \((5, 9\pi/4)\) aur \((5, -7\pi/4)\) teeno ek hi point hain. Matlab ek point ke beshumaar polar naam hote hain. Isi uljhan ko khatam karne ke liye agle topic mein ek standard angle chuna jata hai, jise principal argument kehte hain.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Point \((-3, \pi/2)\) kahan hoga? Pehle \(\pi/2\) ki taraf munh kijiye (seedha upar), phir \(r\) negative hai to 3 units peeche, yaani neeche chaliye. Point negative \(y\)-axis par \((0, -3)\) hai. Kya aap isay \(r\) positive rakh kar likh sakte hain? (Jawab: \((3, 3\pi/2)\) ya \((3, -\pi/2)\).)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
• Polar coordinates \((r, \theta)\): pole \(O\) se distance \(r\), aur polar axis se angle \(\theta\). Pehle \(r\), phir \(\theta\).
• Polar axis aam taur par positive \(x\)-axis hoti hai; angle hamesha counter-clockwise naapte hain.
• \(r > 0\): \(\theta\) ki direction mein \(r\) units chaliye.
• \(r < 0\): ulti direction \(\theta + \pi\) mein \(|r|\) units chaliye.
• \((-r, \theta)\) aur \((r, \theta + \pi)\) ek hi point hain; \(\theta\) mein \(2\pi\) jama ya tafreeq karne se bhi wahi point milta hai.
• \(\pi\) radians \(= 180^{\circ}\); common angles ki table zubani yaad rakhiye.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
• Angle clockwise naapna. Bohat se students ghari ki tarah ghoom jaate hain. Positive angle hamesha polar axis se counter-clockwise hota hai.
• \(r < 0\) ho to point ko \(\theta\) ki direction mein hi laga dena. Yaad rakhiye: negative \(r\) ka matlab "peeche chalo", yaani point \(\theta + \pi\) ki taraf jaata hai.
• Degrees aur radians mila dena: \(\pi/4\) ka matlab \(45^{\circ}\) hai, 0.785 degree nahi. Calculator ka mode bhi check kijiye.
• \((r, \theta)\) ka order ulta likh dena, jaise \((\pi/4, 5)\). Pehle distance, phir angle.
• Yeh samajhna ke point ka sirf ek hi \((r, \theta)\) hota hai. Asal mein beshumaar hote hain; is liye principal argument ki zaroorat padti hai.
